TO: Mr. G. C. Pennell

FROM: T. F. Witner

SUBJECT: MAGNA Advertising Study Results

This provides you with key measures for the MAGNA Advertising Study which evaluated the "Honest Value" campaign versus the "Respect" campaign. Within the test design, ad executions were pitted against POS executions for each campaign. Overall, the ad executions performed at higher levels than the POS executions. Between the two campaign ad executions, "Honest Value" performed slightly better than "Respect", primarily because of its more robust communication via the characters in the advertising. Thus, this report will focus on the findings for the "Honest Value" ad executions among prime prospect smokers who are 25-49 year old male Marlboro smokers having the Low Price with Image mindset. (Recall/key measures for "Respect" versus "Honest Value" ad executions are attached for your reference.)

• Recall/Impact Among Clutter Ads

Within the clutter binder that was exposed to respondents, the MAGNA ad competed against six competitive Savings brands (Bull Durham, Viceroy, DORAL, Pyramid, Bristol and Cambridge). Respondents recalled the MAGNA execution at a high level of 92%. (Unaided recall = 59%; Aided recall = 33%)

The "Honest Value" ad execution garnered first and second mentions as ad most interesting at a higher level than all other clutter ads except Bull Durham.

	FIRST MENTION	SECOND MENTION	TOTAL FIRST/SECOND
MAGNA	23%	23%	46%
Bull Durham	30	13	43
Viceroy	12	15	27
DORAL	8	15	23
Pyramid	8	11	19
Bristol	.10	5	15
Cambridge	7	5	12

• Key Measures

"Honest Value" met the RJR norm for likeability and was parity to likeability scores for Bull Durham and DORAL. "Honest Value" slightly exceeded the RJR norm for positive purchase interest. The positive shift pre-exposure to post-exposure for "Honest Value" was parity to Bull Durham and greater than all other clutter brands.
